Note::is_alpha¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::is_alpha() const

Test Whether Every Character In A Cell Is A Letter¶

is_alpha() reports, for each cell, whether the cell is non-empty and every byte is an ASCII letter (A–Z, a–z). It is one of the character-property predicates, for validating that a field contains only the class of characters you expect before parsing or storing it.

Scope¶

The check is ASCII-only: it uses byte-level classification, so an accented letter (é, ü) or a non-Latin letter causes the cell to fail even though a human would call it alphabetic. If your data has non-ASCII letters, transliterate first (to_ascii), or use a regex predicate with an explicit class.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. An empty cell is false because there is no character to classify. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {"abc", "ABC", "Abc", "abc123", "123", "", "a b", "café"});
const auto mask = n.is_alpha();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]

"abc123" has digits, "123" has no letters, the empty and space cells have none, "a b" has a space, and "café" has the non-ASCII é — all 0.

See Also¶

  • Note::is_alnum / Note::is_digit: the other character-class checks.

  • Note::is_lower / Note::is_upper: letter case checks.

  • Note::contains_any_alpha: “has at least one letter” rather than “is all letters”.
